C-TERMINOLOGY-LANGUAGE-EDITIONS.Summary: Provide separate English and Russian editions of the shared terminology reference, each defining and explaining terms in its own language.

Goals.Goal: Remove Russian definitions and explanatory prose from the English reference and provide a complete Russian reference with the same 71 concepts.
Render and search each portal route from its own language edition and align the corpus indexes and governing descriptions.

Constraints.Constraint: Authority: the user explicitly corrected the language structure: “en holds en defiintions, ru holds ru”. This authorizes the separate editions and their directly affected source-to-portal path. It supersedes the English-only companion constraint and translation exclusion of C-SHARED-TERMINOLOGY; that earlier approved bundle is preserved unchanged as history.

Keep formal institutional wording, equivalent meanings, shared international names, stable record identities, operational requirements and the four subject groups. Neither language receives precedence.
Preserve unrelated workspace work, earlier approved XML contents and decision history.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Rewrite terminology throughout the rest of the Russian corpus, commit, push, deploy, or change operational rules.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Both language directories contain the complete reference with local-language definitions, application, headings and maintenance clauses.
Each reference has 71 entries and equivalent numbered clauses and table structures; the English edition has no Russian definition column or Russian explanatory prose.
The Russian portal uses its Russian source without a fallback notice; both search indexes expose all terms with local-language definitions.
Indexes, Catalog, Vocabulary descriptions, source hashes, regression checks and generated-site validation agree with the separate editions.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Paired semantic review and browser checks of definitions, language switching, search and layouts.
